articles.title: Omnigent is a Meta-Harness For Your AI Agents
articles.summary:
A new open-source agent framework, Omnigent, just launched. It's a meta-harness designed to give you a common orchestration layer over the diverse and growing landscape of coding agents, letting you swap or combine them without rewriting core logic.

This approach abstracts the harness, so you can focus on the task rather than the specific agent implementation. It's a control plane for agents, and it points to a future where we build with a portfolio of specialized AI systems instead of a single, monolithic one.


  
  
  what is a meta-harness


Omnigent isn't another agent; it's a framework

articles.title: I Built a Lightning-Fast Media Downloader and Invoice Generator (And Yes, It Loads Under 1 Second)
articles.summary:
As a web developer, I’ve always been obsessed with web performance. There is nothing more frustrating than opening a utility tool just to see a loading spinner for 5 seconds, followed by three massive pop-up ads and a "Sign up with Google" wall. 

I felt that everyday utility tools should be simple, lightweight, and focused. So, I decided to build Rendexer (https://rendexer.com).

articles.title: Where AI agent test cases come from: synthetic vs. production data
articles.summary:
Before you can evaluate an agent, you need something to evaluate it against. Which test cases you can get depends mostly on timing. Before launch, everything you test with is something your team came up with. After launch, your users start writing test cases for you, whether you collect them or not.

This post compares the main sources and shows how the mix changes as your agent matures. There's a walkthrough video at the end.

articles.title: Magnus AI: a real-time voice assistant that controls my Windows PC
articles.summary:
What I Built


Magnus AI is a voice-first desktop assistant for Windows. You talk to it, and it can:


Open apps and bring windows to the front
Set volume and brightness
Run one-phrase routines like "Work Mode", "Study Mode" and "Night Mode"
Search the web, play YouTube, and set reminders
Read your clipboard
Look at your screen or webcam and help debug code

articles.title: Nonobench: an open benchmark of 49 LLMs on nonogram puzzles, public and open source [P]
articles.summary: Nonobench measures how well LLMs solve nonograms (picross). Each model gets the row and column clues once and returns the full grid. No tools, one attempt per puzzle. Method: - Standard mode: 30 puzzles from 5x5 to 15x15 (from the Nonograms dataset by Moyà-Alcover, CC BY 4.0). - Hard mode: ten random 20x20s, each checked to have a single solution. Five can't be solved by line logic alone. Random fills avoid picture puzzles that models can guess. - 130 variants across reasoning effort levels, run through OpenRouter and pinned to each lab's own endpoint where possible.
